proposed_from.topic: Tensor support saturation for complete causal identification under structural zeros. For a finite acyclic SCM with one mutually independent finite latent root per bidirected-clique district, known graph and supplied realizable exact observational support S, characterize uniform identification of P_x(Y) over every same-law model on the relative interior of S. Prove that first-forbidden-prefix saturation yields the unique maximal Cartesian response support; recover supported district Q-signatures; show identification iff the target response indicator belongs to their tensor row span; compile success into one rational functional with denominators positive throughout the face, and compile failure into strictly positive rational same-support, same-law twins differing in the query. Derive multinomial influence-function inference on fixed epsilon-interiors and a support-scoped dosearch compiler. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: forbidden-prefix deletion, positive-prefix Q-factor telescoping, and tensor row-span separation were derived as a non-QE proof spine. Exact checks cover 165 realizable binary-IV masks with 134 identified and 190 negative queries, all 255 frontdoor supports with 336 identified and 144 negative queries, and 463 alternating-district support images plus 64 tensor queries; the intervention ledger rejects the diagonal-bow substitution and derives the five-cell IV identity. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: compile the product-preserving SAT-SID rules, including signed intermediate expressions, into the bounded tensor/Q-factor certificate language and independently verify the maximal-support proof and novelty against quasi-Markovian credal networks. EARLY KILL TEST: attack first-forbidden-prefix saturation, then require rejection of Y=X after do(X=1) in the diagonal bow and derivation of the five-cell IV formula through the identified do(Z=1) kernel. The paper must therefore present maximal support, the uniform quantifier, and the rational converse as the theorem-level delta rather than claim novelty for districtwise linearization itself.","strict_delta":"The proposed kernel is a law-uniform necessary-and-sufficient theorem on an arbitrary realizable exact observational support face. It first derives the unique maximal Cartesian response support from forbidden prefixes, then reduces every same-law fiber to supported district signatures, and finally gives both a common rational formula and rational positive same-support countermodels. The closest credal result is an exact numerical representation, not this symbolic singleton characterization, while the closest positivity result is formula-specific and sufficient rather than complete.","unoccupied_pair":"No inspected primary source combines exact joint-support saturation with a tensor row-span iff criterion and constructive rational interior separation."}

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction on pp. 1--2, Theorem 5.1 on p. 7, Section 7.2, and the Conclusion on p. 9 were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace formula-specific positive-prefix cancellation by a support-global response-type saturation and then test constancy on every same-law fiber.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for \(\text{structural zeros}+\text{causal identification}+\text{response types}+\text{tensor row span}\) and \(\text{quasi-Markovian}+\text{exact support}\) found numerical credal and polynomial programs but no face-uniform tensor criterion.
seed_details.kernel: For every realizable support face in the finite independent-district-root class, uniform identification of \(P_x(y)\) is equivalent to membership of its intervention-response indicator in the tensor product of support-restricted district-signature row spaces.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Hwang et al. because Theorem 5.1 already recovers zero-aware district factors.
seed_details.rebuttal: Theorem 5.1 is a sufficient, formula-local cancellation result and expressly leaves necessity and positivity-aware identification open; it neither constructs the maximal response support nor proves a face-uniform converse.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction on pp. 1--2, the strictly positive empirical-law convention and local linear constraints on pp. 5--8, Theorem 2, and the Conclusion on p. 11 were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace conditional constraints at every parent configuration by deletion at the first supported prefix whose extension is forbidden.
seed_details.destination_search: The support-saturation and quasi-Markovian credal-network search found no theorem giving a unique largest Cartesian response support for an arbitrary realizable exact support mask.
seed_details.kernel: First-forbidden-prefix deletion is necessary and sufficient for the unique maximal product of district response supports compatible with a realizable observational support face.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate zero propagation from Algorithm 2 of Zaffalon et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: Zero propagation gives necessity; the nonlocal sufficiency that every surviving cross-district tuple remains inside the support, and hence uniqueness of a largest Cartesian chart, is not in that algorithm.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, canonical response construction in Section 3, Proposition 2 and Theorem 1 in Section 4, and the critiques and future-work sections were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace numerical extrema of a multilinear same-law fiber by a rational null-space perturbation that stays in the positive product simplex.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact-witness search found classical hedge witnesses and numerical sharp bounds, but no universal strictly positive rational same-support pair tied to failure of a support-restricted tensor criterion.
seed_details.kernel: Every failed tensor certificate has two rational product response laws, positive on the same maximal supports, with the same exact-support observational law and distinct query values.
seed_details.rebuttal: Ordinary separation does not preserve the nonlinear product parameterization, exact observational support, strict positivity, or rationality; the required one-root perturbation and other-root spanning argument supplies all four.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction on pp. 1--2, the search-state construction, Theorems 2--3 on pp. 16--17, and the Conclusion on p. 36 were inspected. The first changed proof step is to attach exact-support domains and signed product certificates to every search state before applying probability transformations.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search located positivity-aware formula checking and context-specific search calculi, but no complete rule system normalizing support-face derivations to bounded tensor certificates.
seed_details.kernel: A finite support-indexed rule system is sound and complete for the declared model class and every successful derivation normalizes to a denominator-safe tensor certificate.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a software extension of do-search.
seed_details.rebuttal: The contribution would be a calculus-level completeness and normalization theorem for signed product expressions, not an implementation feature.
seed_details.disposition: kept as the first-class open question because the normalization proof remains unresolved

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Proposition 1, Section 4 and Proposition 8, Theorems 1--2, and the concluding empirical section were inspected. The paper's state constraints specify variable cardinalities; the first changed step is to condition instead on the exact support of the observational law and propagate its forbidden cells through independent district response types.
seed_details.destination_search: The search confirmed that the 2025 result rules out gains from cardinality information alone, not gains from a supplied exact observational support face.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize exactly when an observational support constraint adds identification beyond a graph, separating mere state-cardinality restrictions from exact-law support restrictions.
seed_details.red_team: Contradicted by Chen and Darwiche because state constraints alone do not improve identification.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their state constraint fixes which values a variable can take, while the proposed object fixes which joint observational cells have positive mass; these are different restrictions, and the theorem would state their boundary explicitly.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because it is a corollary-level framing of the tensor kernel

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction on pp. 1--3, Theorem 8 and its pathwise-differentiation proof, and the Conclusion on p. 36 were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace a fixed positive ADMG law by a triangular multinomial sequence approaching a face where the identifying functional itself changes.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found influence-function theory for graph-derived functionals and overlap-robust alternative interventions, but not a local asymptotic experiment across an identification-changing support boundary.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the Gaussian, weak-denominator, and support-switching limits of a rational support-face estimator as the smallest licensed prefix probability tends to zero.
seed_details.red_team: Routine delta method under weak overlap.
seed_details.rebuttal: At the boundary the support mask and hence the identification criterion changes, so the local experiment is not a fixed-functional weak-overlap calculation.
seed_details.disposition: deferred because the changing-support experiment requires a separate paper

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The sharp polynomial-program theorem and the paper's confidence-region construction were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace a fixed exact support mask by a confidence family of masks and optimize the tensor criterion across that family.
seed_details.destination_search: No located paper combines sampling uncertainty about structural zeros with graph-native sharp bounds over support masks.
seed_details.kernel: Construct valid and, where attainable, sharp causal bounds when observed zero cells may be sampling zeros, using a confidence set over support faces.
seed_details.red_team: Already covered by adding multinomial confidence constraints to autobounds.
seed_details.rebuttal: That construction is available as a generic polynomial program, but an explicit union-of-faces certificate and uniform coverage result would still differ; the likely gain is computational rather than foundational.
seed_details.disposition: not selected because the novelty delta is narrower than the complete-identification kernel

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Definitions 2--3, the arithmetic-circuit construction, Theorem 1 and its Appendix proof, the fixed-distribution examples, and the Conclusion were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace sufficient invariant cuts for a fixed numerical law by a symbolic invariant test uniform over a support face.
seed_details.destination_search: The circuit literature contains sufficient invariant-cut certificates, but the searched sources do not give a face-uniform necessary-and-sufficient symbolic test.
seed_details.kernel: An arithmetic circuit for a causal query is constant on every compatible fiber over a support face if and only if its multilinear coefficient tensor lies in the supported district row span.
seed_details.red_team: A restatement of constrained identifiability in circuit notation.
seed_details.rebuttal: The iff coefficient test and uniform symbolic functional would be new, but this framing is algebraically equivalent to the selected tensor seed and therefore not a distinct angle.
seed_details.disposition: merged into the selected seed rather than counted as a separate contribution

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Theorem 4.1 and proof, and the Conclusion were inspected. The first changed proof step is to replace objective-degree reduction by a rank computation exploiting the number and response width of intervened districts.
seed_details.destination_search: The adjacent complexity literature gives multilinear-program degree reductions and NP-hardness, but no output-sensitive complexity bound for support-face tensor certificates.
seed_details.kernel: Bound certificate construction by the intervened-district response width without materializing the full Kronecker matrix.
seed_details.red_team: A standard sparse Kronecker linear-algebra implementation result.
seed_details.rebuttal: A genuine fixed-parameter tractability theorem might survive, but the present evidence does not yet separate it from routine tensor contraction.
seed_details.disposition: dropped after the red-team objection remained unresolved
